page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v3 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance belonging to the LASv3 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

A primary feature of the L16as_v3 is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 4004 GB NVMe SSD, and its capability for Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, alongside average multi-core CPU performance. Memory bandwidth tests reveal a notable tradeoff: while cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, falling into the bottom 25 percent of tested hardware.

The server delivers average performance across a wide range of workloads, including database operations, Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It also shows strong text generation speeds for small language models. Given its high local NVMe storage density and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the L16as_v3 offers qualitative cost efficiency for storage-intensive workloads and database hosting that require high-capacity local scratch space without the need for dedicated GPU acceleration.
